habitat: Groups or flocks on marshy ground, dams, shorelines, agricultural land and rubbish dumps, and in breeding colonies of other large birds.
summary: A common resident. The decurved bill, head, neck and legs are black, and the rest of the plumage is white. Loose fluffy plumes show on the back at close range. The immature has the black head and neck speckled white, and the front of the neck white. Newman does not describe the voice. The Kemp name Sacred Ibis and the code NB were left unchanged.

upperparts.pattern: Loose fluffy plumes on the back show at close range.

head.pattern: Black head and neck speckled white. The front of the neck is white.

viewNotes.note: White body, black head and neck, and a decurved black bill.
White, with loose fluffy plumes on the back.
White body and black flight contrast are not separately described.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: Newman does not describe the voice. The grade A file is a chick begging call from Grahamstown. The filename is XC309388-sacred ibis chick.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. It is migratory to some degree within Africa and most common in southern Africa in summer. The voice is not described. The grade A recording is a chick begging call from the Eastern Cape. The iNaturalist account has no display name, so the login agujaceratops is credited. The Kemp name Sacred Ibis and the code NB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^4=16 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 8–32.
